auditMetadata.notes: Forensic audit of harbour vessels register. Explicitly separated PRE_ATTACK_POSITION, ATTACK_POSITION, SINKING_POSITION, and WRECK_POSITION_MODERN_SURVEY to eliminate confusion between modern wreck surveys and 09:30 harbour dispositions. Re-authenticated casualties, bomb hits, and movement states.

entities.name: USS Peary (DD-226)
entities.commandingOfficer: Lieutenant Commander John M. Bermingham, USN (Killed)
entities.movementState: Underway under attack, executing high-speed evasive manoeuvres in harbour

preAttackPosition.description: Underway in main channel, preparing to sortie or maneuver to anchorage

attackPosition.description: Engaged in violent evasive maneuvering in mid-harbour while repeatedly attacked by dive bombers

sinkingPosition.description: Sank stern-first after sustaining 5 bomb hits; anti-aircraft guns fired until decks submerged

wreckPositionModernSurvey.description: Surveyed wreck lying on seabed at 27m depth in Darwin Harbour; marked by navigation buoy and protected historic shipwreck
wreckPositionModernSurvey.surveySource: Australian Hydrographic Office / Northern Territory Heritage Register

entities.damageDescription: Struck by five bombs (two in fire rooms, one in galley, one on aft deckhouse, one on fantail). Anti-aircraft gunners (including Machine Gunner First Class Mitchel) continued firing until water reached deck. Sank stern-first.
entities.notes: Heaviest single loss of American life in Australian waters during WW2. Wreck location confirmed by post-war hydrographic and diving surveys.

entities.name: USS William B. Preston (AVD-7)
entities.movementState: Underway in harbour tending PBY flying boats; maneuvered into open sea

preAttackPosition.description: Moored or drifting in seaplane anchorage tending VP-22 Catalina flying boats

attackPosition.description: Struck aft while getting underway; lost rudder control; steered using twin propellers into outer harbour

entities.damageDescription: Bomb struck aft deckhouse, penetrating to mess hall, killing 14 crewmen and wounding 2; lost steering control, steered by engines into outer harbour.
entities.notes: Surviving ship got underway despite steering casualty; two PBY aircraft in vicinity destroyed by strafing.

entities.name: MV Neptuna
entities.movementState: Berthed alongside Stokes Hill Wharf pier face

preAttackPosition.description: Tied to outer berth of timber Stokes Hill Wharf, actively discharging depth charges and munitions

attackPosition.description: Hit by two bombs while berthed alongside wharf; crew and waterside workers attempted fire-fighting until depth charges ignited

sinkingPosition.description: Catastrophic magazine and depth-charge explosion severed wharf structure; hull burned and capsized at wharf berth

wreckPositionModernSurvey.description: Wreck cleared and extensively salvaged post-war by Carl Atkinson and Fujita Salvage Company (1959–1961) to clear modern port navigation lanes
wreckPositionModernSurvey.surveySource: Darwin Port Authority / Northern Territory Archives

entities.damageDescription: Moored on the outer berth of Stokes Hill Wharf unloading 100 depth charges and 200 tons of high-explosive ammunition. Hit by two bombs; caught fire. While being fought by crew and wharf labourers, magazines and depth charges detonated in an immense catastrophic explosion that destroyed the ship and severed the wharf deck.
entities.notes: Coordinates remain UNRESOLVED pending integration of 1942 Stokes Hill Wharf engineering survey (NAA: A2633). Position is known to be alongside the 1942 pier face, but cannot be assigned coordinates without inventing 1942 wharf geometry.

entities.name: MV Zealandia
entities.vesselType: Passenger-Cargo Liner & Troop Transport (6,683 gross tons)

preAttackPosition.description: Anchored in central harbour roadstead at designated Berth 12 (1.4km south of Stokes Hill Wharf)

attackPosition.description: Struck in hatch No. 3 by high-explosive bomb; dense smoke, abandon ship ordered

sinkingPosition.description: Burned fiercely, settled to the harbour floor on an even keel at approx 13:30

wreckPositionModernSurvey.description: Wreck surveyed at 19m depth (12° 28.883' S, 130° 51.048' E); partially salvaged by Fujita Salvage (1960); remains prominent historical dive site
wreckPositionModernSurvey.surveySource: Northern Territory Heritage Branch Shipwrecks Register / Australian National Shipwreck Database

entities.damageDescription: Struck by bomb in hatch No. 3; caught fire. Abandon ship ordered; burned fiercely and sank in harbour.
entities.notes: Anchorage location recorded in Lowe Commission exhibits; wreck position subsequently verified by diving operations.

entities.name: USAT Meigs
entities.movementState: Anchored in harbour loaded with munitions, Bren gun carriers, and aviation fuel

preAttackPosition.description: Anchored in southern reach of main harbour anchorage

attackPosition.description: Attacked by both horizontal and dive-bombers; cargo of munitions and vehicles ignited

sinkingPosition.description: Engulfed in flames and ammunition explosions, foundered during the afternoon

wreckPositionModernSurvey.description: Largest transport wreck in harbour; surveyed at 18m depth, masts originally protruded at low water
wreckPositionModernSurvey.surveySource: Northern Territory Heritage Branch Shipwrecks Register

entities.damageDescription: Struck by multiple bombs from horizontal and dive bombers; engulfed in flames, sank in harbour.
entities.notes: One of the largest vessels in port; wreck remains a known dive site in Darwin Harbour.

entities.name: USAT Mauna Loa
entities.movementState: Anchored in harbour loaded with ammunition

preAttackPosition.description: Anchored in western anchorage sector loaded with 500-lb bombs and ammunition

attackPosition.description: Two direct bomb hits penetrated through cargo holds into ammunition compartments

sinkingPosition.description: Sank in harbour at approx 12:10; crew successfully abandoned ship under fire

wreckPositionModernSurvey.description: Surveyed wreck lying at 18m depth, superstructure demolished post-war for navigational safety
wreckPositionModernSurvey.surveySource: Northern Territory Heritage Branch Shipwrecks Register

entities.damageDescription: Struck by two bombs through cargo holds; abandoned and sank in harbour.
entities.notes: Anchorage position recorded in Lowe Commission exhibits.

entities.name: British Motorist
entities.movementState: Anchored in harbour discharging fuel oil

preAttackPosition.description: Anchored near Stokes Hill discharging fuel oil to naval installations

attackPosition.description: Hit by two bombs; oil cargo ignited, creating a massive black smoke plume

sinkingPosition.description: Burned fiercely, capsized and settled on seabed during the afternoon

wreckPositionModernSurvey.description: Wreck surveyed and extensively salvaged post-war by Fujita Salvage (1960)

entities.damageDescription: Hit by two bombs; caught fire, capsized and sank in harbour waters near wharf approach.
entities.notes: Wreck salvaged partially post-war; position charted on Admiralty Chart 925.

entities.name: USAT Admiral Halstead
entities.movementState: Anchored in harbour carrying 14,000 drums of 100-octane aviation gasoline

preAttackPosition.description: Anchored in harbour loaded with high-octane drum fuel

attackPosition.description: Damaged by near misses and heavy strafing; heroic action by crew and artillerymen prevented cargo explosion

entities.damageDescription: Shaken severely by near misses; machine-gunned; crew heroically jettisoned damaged drum cargo and prevented catastrophic fire.
entities.notes: Cargo saved through courageous action of crew and US artillerymen onboard.

entities.name: AHS Manunda (2/1st Australian Hospital Ship)
entities.nationality: Royal Australian Army Medical Corps / Adelaide Steamship Co.
entities.movementState: Anchored in designated hospital ship anchorage

preAttackPosition.description: Anchored in designated white-painted Red Cross safety anchorage

attackPosition.description: Direct bomb hit through bridge structure into medical accommodations; near misses holed hull plates

entities.damageDescription: Clearly painted white with broad green stripe and red crosses illuminated. Struck by a bomb directly through navigation bridge to medical quarters; multiple near-misses holed hull. 12 staff killed including Sister Margaret de Mestre (AANS) and medical orderlies; 19 seriously wounded. Ship survived and treated hundreds of wounded.
entities.notes: Sister Margaret de Mestre was the first Australian military nurse killed on active service on Australian territory.

entities.name: HMAS Swan (U42)
entities.movementState: Underway in harbour at action stations

preAttackPosition.description: Underway in harbour at action stations

attackPosition.description: Targeted by eight separate dive-bombing runs; sustained near misses and heavy strafing while firing continuous AA barrages

entities.damageDescription: Targeted by eight separate dive-bombing runs; sustained near misses and heavy strafing. 3 killed, 19 wounded. Fired continuous anti-aircraft barrages.
entities.notes: Primary RAN warship defending harbour; maneuvered aggressively throughout first raid.

entities.name: HMAS Platypus (A3)
entities.movementState: Moored in harbour near Stokes Hill Wharf

preAttackPosition.description: Moored at naval buoy off Stokes Hill Wharf

attackPosition.description: Near miss ruptured hull plates and flooded engine room; 3 crew killed

entities.damageDescription: Near miss ruptured hull plates and flooded engine room; 3 crew killed. Remained afloat providing repair and support services.
entities.notes: Depot ship base for local RAN flotilla.

entities.name: HMAS Deloraine (J232)
entities.movementState: Underway in harbour at high speed

preAttackPosition.description: Underway at high speed maneuvering in open harbour

attackPosition.description: Avoided bomb hits through high-speed evasive maneuvering while firing 12-pounder and Oerlikons

entities.damageDescription: Avoided bomb hits through high-speed evasive maneuvering; engaged aircraft with 12-pounder and Oerlikon guns.
entities.notes: Famous for having sunk Japanese submarine I-124 off Darwin on 20 January 1942.

entities.name: SS Barossa
entities.movementState: Berthed at the main (Stokes Hill) wharf; towed clear and beached nearby

preAttackPosition.description: Berthed at the main wharf with an oil lighter alongside, on the other side of the pier from MV Neptuna

attackPosition.description: Bombed and set on fire while berthed at the main wharf; the tug Wato towed the burning oil lighter clear, then took Barossa in tow clear of the burning Neptuna

entities.damageDescription: Bombed and set on fire while berthed at the main wharf; towed clear of the burning Neptuna by the tug Wato and beached nearby, where her cargo burnt out.
entities.notes: Later salvaged and towed to Brisbane (Lewis 2002). Position at the 1942 wharf follows the same rule as MV Neptuna: the 1942 wharf/berth geometry is unresolved in canon, so no coordinate is drawn.

beachingPosition.description: Beached near the wharf after being towed clear; exact site not recorded in the cited sources

canonCorrections.reason: Previous entry placed Barossa at anchor in the northern anchorage at a coordinate that falls on land, and described near-miss hull damage. Both are contradicted by the cited sources, which place her berthed at the main wharf, set on fire, towed clear and beached.

previousValues.movementState: Anchored in harbour; beached after damage

attackPosition.description: Severe hull leakage caused by near misses; captain ordered ship run aground to prevent sinking in fairway

previousValues.damageDescription: Near misses caused heavy hull leakage; beached on a sandbank to avoid sinking in the main channel.

entities.name: Kelat (Coal Storage Hulk)
entities.vesselType: Iron Sailing Vessel / Stationary Coal Hulk (1,849 tons)

preAttackPosition.description: Moored in central harbour as coaling hulk

attackPosition.description: Sprung hull plates and rivet failures from concussion of near-miss bombs

sinkingPosition.description: Slowly settled under persistent flooding, sinking on 24 February 1942

wreckPositionModernSurvey.description: Iron hull surveyed on seabed at 15m depth
wreckPositionModernSurvey.surveySource: Northern Territory Heritage Branch Shipwrecks Register

entities.damageDescription: Plates sprung by near misses; slowly settled and sank five days later.
entities.notes: Former iron clipper ship built in 1881 used as coaling depot.

entities.name: HMAS Kangaroo
entities.movementState: Moored on the anti-submarine boom gate station

preAttackPosition.description: Moored at anti-submarine indicator boom net gate between Dudley Point and West Point

attackPosition.description: Attacked by dive bombers at the boom gate; near misses caused splinter damage

entities.damageDescription: Attacked by dive bombers at the boom gate; 1 crew member killed (Stoker A.J. Couchman).
entities.notes: Operated the boom gate vessel at the entrance to Darwin Harbour.
